title: RAW UNREVIEWED: visually grounded argument transport within known r/l phrase families separates participant agreement from fixed collocation
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. Combine transferred known r/l phrase families with independently coded object/label hosts. Restrict the hypothesis to the already licensed complete phrase families rather than inventing a universal suffix rule. A participant-conditioned construction must predict which written dependency changes when the grounded argument changes while the phrase and register are controlled; a lexical-collocation account has no shared participant dependency. No ending, object name or operation is translated.

design.mechanism: A compiler may retain conventional learned phrase templates while varying their forms to agree with the participant referred to. Another compiler may simply copy lexicalized phrase bundles. The existing mixture of transferable familiar phrases and failed unseen stem-pair generalization makes these distinct authoring mechanisms worth comparing without assuming productive general morphology.
design.unit: Only GDT915/GDT916 known ordered stem-pair families, complete native occurrences, and independently annotated GDT791 label-host and record-owner observations. All four RR/RL/LR/LL cells and all eligible complete occurrences must remain visible; no invented new stem combinations.

positive_inputs.fact: The retained A_SEEN association transfers for familiar stem pairs; the B_NEW_LICENSED result does not establish new-pair concordance. This constrains the unit to familiar phrase constructions.

A lossless inventory distinguishes local labels from running prose and physical owner regimes; three pages have deeper component/panel annotation. Those physical distinctions are independent of an English lexical interpretation.

design.contrast: PARTICIPANT_FEATURE: a fixed known-phrase construction indexes a property of its bound participant; LEXICAL_BUNDLE: the known phrase chooses a stored r/l pattern independent of participant; RECORD_RENDERER: position/hand/record changes select the pattern. Every candidate pays for its binding rule and whole-form exceptions.
design.prediction: Nominate a crossed set with the same licensed phrase used for different independently fixed participant classes and with a class reused in a different position/record. Participant-feature predicts the family pattern and which written downstream argument must share that feature across both contrasts. Lexical-bundle predicts stability with phrase identity; record-renderer predicts stability with the record variables. Anonymous class labels may be permuted, but moving a dependency from the visibly bound participant to a different participant must change predictions. This can constrain agreement versus collocation without naming the class in English.
design.falsifier: A specified participant account fails if the same independently bound participant class requires opposite feature assignments in matched complete contexts, or if its predicted downstream agreement consistently follows a different written argument. Label proximity, picture-wide topic and correlated class/hand distributions cannot count as the required crossed observation.
design.smallest_next_step: Prepare one compact frozen inventory from already existing known-family IDs and owner metadata, counting actual crossed cells without opening new manuscript content. If there is a real crossed set, manually author the three full dependency accounts for its complete previously exposed records and retain every mismatch before any scoring code. No universal suffix fit or new graph decoder.
design.predecessors: GDT916 remains a failed new-pair transfer test and its window/suffix/partition are not retuned. IDEA78 supplies a generic selectional-class hypothesis; IDEA50 warns that argument reversal alone does not force a marker reversal; this proposal instead asks whether an independently grounded participant predicts the known phrase feature across a controlled crossover. IDEA891/892 concern visual-property recombination/global relational grounding, not a fixed licensed phrase inventory and a downstream participant-agreement consequence. Existing IP021 nonlocal count confounding must be checked before selection. GDT981 REPORT read: its fixed 22-family state-carry F is contradicted, R has only one direction-mobile leaf and zero independently bound meaning. This proposal is not a changed state-carry direction or altered intervening-word rule: the contrasted dependency is on an independently coded participant, versus phrase and record rendering. All four old chains and their counterexamples remain; none supplies participant binding.
design.uncertainty: Physical owner classes are not automatically grammatical arguments or semantic classes. The overlap and crossed capacity have not been inspected and may be empty. Even success would establish only a conditional construction-level dependency, not r/l meaning, gender, number, or a lexical translation. Exact whole profiles and claim-bearing counterexamples remain mandatory before assigning any word. Reader channels separate; sealed/reserved data remain closed.
